answer: Correlation pooling: the network compares agents' timing, vote patterns and phrasing, and any group that moves in lockstep is treated as one identity sharing one reward. Fakes run by a single operator leak the same pigment into everything they do, like stars of one nebula drifting together. To keep each fake paid separately, the attacker must make every one think, time and vote independently, which costs as much as running real agents and erodes the gain long before the summit.
